residencyRequirements.description: Either party must be domiciled in England and Wales, or have been habitually resident for at least one year immediately before the application (Domicile and Matrimonial Proceedings Act 1973, s.5(2)).

waitingPeriod.description: 20-week reflection period from the date the application is issued to the Conditional Order (Matrimonial Causes Act 1973, s.1(5), as substituted by the Divorce, Dissolution and Separation Act 2020). After the Conditional Order, a further 6-week gap before the Final Order can be applied for (MCA 1973, s.1(4)(b)).

noFault.name: Irretrievable Breakdown
noFault.description: The sole ground for divorce since April 2022. The applicant (or joint applicants) provides a statement that the marriage has irretrievably broken down. No need to prove fault, adultery, or separation.
noFault.statute: Matrimonial Causes Act 1973, s.1(1), as substituted by the Divorce, Dissolution and Separation Act 2020, s.1

basic.name: Online Application (or Form D8)
basic.description: Application for a divorce, dissolution, or (judicial) separation — filed online via the HMCTS portal or on paper using Form D8

basic.name: Form D80A-D80E (Statement in Support)
basic.description: Historical forms for proving grounds — no longer required under no-fault divorce (post-April 2022) except for judicial separation

basic.name: Form A (Financial Remedy)
basic.description: Application for a financial order under MCA 1973; needed if financial remedy is sought

legalCitations.description: No-fault divorce — single ground of irretrievable breakdown, in force 6 April 2022
Governs financial remedy orders (s.23-25A) — lump sum, property adjustment, periodical payments, pension sharing
Welfare of children — s.1 welfare principle, s.8 child arrangements orders
Statutory child maintenance — calculated by CMS or agreed privately

filingFees.notes: Filing fee for divorce application (increased from £612 to £628 on 13 July 2026 — gov.uk / HMCTS EX50). Fee remission (Help with Fees / HWF) available for those on low income or receiving certain benefits.

childSupportGuidelines.guidelines: Child Maintenance Service (CMS) — gross income formula
childSupportGuidelines.notes: CMS uses gross income from HMRC data. Basic rate: 12% for 1 child, 16% for 2, 19% for 3+. Parents may agree private arrangements (family-based arrangements) instead.

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: Court considers all circumstances including income, earning capacity, financial needs, standard of living, age, duration of marriage, disability, and contributions. No fixed formula — discretionary.

effectiveDateRule: The divorce is finalised when the Final Order is made. The Conditional Order can be applied for after the 20-week reflection period. The Final Order can be applied for 6 weeks after the Conditional Order.
certificateNote: A copy of the Final Order (formerly Decree Absolute) can be obtained from the court. It serves as proof that the marriage has been dissolved.
jointApplicationNote: Joint applications are available under the 2020 Act. Both parties apply together and neither is solely responsible for the application.
